answer: A congestion-pricing toll gate at the identity summit charges every new agent a variable entry fee that rises with local registration density, forcing sybils into costly bursts. Like a willow bending traffic around a closed lane, the gate reroutes cheap identities into throttled queues where sustained proof-of-work latency makes mass registration unprofitable. The trellis of trust links each identity to sponsor capacity, so a sybil swarm exhausts shared bandwidth and triggers backpressure, though colluding sponsors can still absorb cost until the sponsor graph itself congests.
